hotel.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 13:00. Take the Magical Express or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber) to your boutique stay near Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Pick up a resort map and plan your week. Walk around the hotel grounds and nearby Disney Springs area to get your bearings — entry to Disney Springs is FREE.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Disney Springs for a relaxed first evening. Explore the shops, street performers, and atmosphere at no park-ticket cost. Grab dinner at a budget-friendly spot and enjoy the Disney magic without spending on park admission.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during your layover — grab a sandwich or snack from an airport grab-and-go shop to save money.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and affordable meal at a Disney Springs counter-service spot like Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza or Earl of Sandwich — meals around $10–$14.
meals.dinner: Dine at The BOATHOUSE or grab budget bites at D-Luxe Burger or Chicken Guy! at Disney Springs — budget around $12–$18 per person. Share plates where possible.

day_by_day.notes: Do NOT purchase park tickets for Day 1 — save your park days. Disney Springs is completely free to enter and a great way to ease into the Disney experience. Stock up on snacks and water bottles at a nearby Publix or Walmart (use Uber/Lyft or the hotel shuttle) to save money throughout the week. Bring refillable water bottles — Disney allows outside food and non-alcoholic drinks in parks.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — arrive at Magic Kingdom when the gates open (typically 8:00 or 9:00 AM). Take advantage of Early Entry if your hotel qualifies (Disney Resort guests get 30 minutes early access). Head straight to Tomorrowland for TRON Lightcycle / Run and Space Mountain before crowds build. Then hit Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and Haunted Mansion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fantasyland — ride Seven Dwarfs Mine Train (use Lightning Lane if budget allows, otherwise join standby early). Visit Prince Charming Regal Carrousel and 'it's a small world.' Take a mid-afternoon break back at the hotel during peak heat hours (1–3 PM) to rest and save on in-park food costs. Return refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for the evening. Watch the iconic Festival of Fantasy Parade and end the night with the spectacular EPCOT Forever or Magic Kingdom's Happily Ever After fireworks show (check current schedule). Fireworks are included with park admission — no extra cost!

meals.breakfast: Eat a filling breakfast at your hotel or from snacks you pre-purchased at a grocery store. Oatmeal, fruit, or granola bars — keep it light and cheap.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — excellent budget-friendly counter service. Try the clam chowder or fish and chips. Around $12–$15 per person.
meals.dinner: Pinocchio Village Haus near 'it's a small world' — flatbreads and pasta dishes at moderate prices (~$14–$18). Or bring in a packed dinner from your hotel to save significantly.

day_by_day.notes: Magic Kingdom is the most iconic Disney park and worth a full day. Purchase tickets in advance online — Disney tickets are cheaper when bought ahead and avoid day-of price surges. Rope drop (arriving before park opening) is the single best budget strategy to avoid long waits without paying for Lightning Lane. Bring your refillable water bottle — free water is available at any quick-service location upon request.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at EPCOT. Arrive at rope drop and head immediately to Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane — book at 7 AM via the My Disney Experience app). Then ride Test Track and Soarin' Around the World before lines grow. Explore Future World East and West pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the World Showcase — explore the international pavilions of Mexico, Norway, China, Italy, France, and more. This is one of Disney's most unique and culturally rich experiences. Many pavilions have free entertainment, architecture, and atmosphere to enjoy. Ride Frozen Ever After in the Norway Pavilion. Check out live cultural performances around the World Showcase Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's nighttime spectacular — currently 'EPCOT Forever' or 'Luminous The Symphony of Us' (verify current show for 2027). The fireworks and water show over World Showcase Lagoon is breathtaking and included with admission. Grab a budget snack from one of the World Showcase food stands to enjoy during the show.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed breakfast from hotel supplies — yogurt, fruit, granola bars eaten before entering the park.
meals.lunch: Lotus Blossom Café in the China Pavilion — affordable rice bowls and egg rolls around $11–$14. Or grab a quick snack from Les Halles Boulangerie-Patisserie in France for a budget croissant and coffee.
meals.dinner: Tangierine Café in the Morocco Pavilion — excellent budget-friendly Mediterranean food (shawarma, falafel, hummus platters) for around $13–$17 per person. One of EPCOT's best-kept budget secrets.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase is essentially a free cultural experience once inside the park. Avoid expensive sit-down restaurants in EPCOT — the counter-service options around World Showcase are diverse, delicious, and far more affordable. The International Food & Wine Festival (typically fall) is not in June, but EPCOT may have other seasonal festivals — check the Disney website for 2027 events.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios day! Arrive at rope drop and go directly to Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance — one of Disney's most immersive and popular attractions. Then ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run. Head to Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land before lines get too long.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toy Story Land fully — ride Alien Swirling Saucers and enjoy the theming. Head to Sunset Boulevard and ride Rock 'n' Roller Coaster and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. Watch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (free with admission, check show times). Take a mid-afternoon hotel break if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return for the Star Wars: A Galactic Spectacular fireworks show over Hollywood Studios (check 2027 schedule). Walk through Galaxy's Edge one more time at night — the atmosphere is magical after dark. End the night with a stroll through the beautifully themed Batuu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pre-packed snacks.
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — one of Hollywood Studios' most popular and affordable counter-service spots. Toasted sandwiches and lunch boxes around $11–$14.
meals.dinner: Backlot Express near Echo Lake — burgers, sandwiches, and salads at budget-friendly prices ($12–$15). Or Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge for themed but reasonably priced meals (~$13–$17).

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios has some of Disney's most thrilling rides. The virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance fills up fast — set an alarm and book at exactly 7:00 AM on the My Disney Experience app. Galaxy's Edge is worth extra time even just for the immersive theming — it costs nothing extra to walk around and soak in the atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day — sleep in! This is your mid-trip break to recharge. Spend the morning at your hotel pool (most Disney-area hotels have pools). Relax, swim, and enjoy the downtime. Alternatively, take a free Disney bus to Disney Springs for morning shopping and browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Disney Springs for free afternoon entertainment. Browse the World of Disney store, watch street performers, and explore the unique shops and restaurants. Check out the LEGO store where kids can build for free at the play tables. Visit the Splitsville Luxury Lanes if budget allows ($15–$20 for bowling) or just enjoy the lakeside atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Optional: Visit a Disney Resort hotel lobby for free. The Grand Floridian, Wilderness Lodge, and Polynesian Village Resort lobbies are stunning and open to all guests. Take the free Disney monorail or boat between resorts — it's a fun, free activity with great views. End the evening with dinner back near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast — use your grocery store supplies for a proper sit-down meal in your room. Eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Grab a casual lunch at Disney Springs — Chicken Guy! by Guy Fieri offers affordable chicken tenders and sandwiches around $10–$13.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in your room if you have kitchen facilities, or pick up affordable groceries for a picnic-style dinner. Alternatively, enjoy a budget meal at a nearby non-Disney restaurant on Hotel Plaza Blvd — Burger King, Subway, or a local pizza place to save significantly.

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is essential on a week-long Disney trip, especially in June heat. Temperatures in Orlando in June regularly reach 90°F+ with high humidity. Pacing yourself prevents burnout and keeps morale high for the final park days. Use this day to do laundry if needed, recharge devices, and reorganize your park bags.

day_by_day.morning: Animal Kingdom day! Arrive at rope drop — Animal Kingdom opens early (sometimes 7:00 or 8:00 AM) and is best experienced in the morning before the heat peaks. Head directly to Avatar Flight of Passage in Pandora — The World of Avatar. This is consistently one of Disney's highest-rated rides. Then ride Na'vi River Journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa — ride Kilimanjaro Safaris (morning and late afternoon are best for animal activity). Watch the Festival of the Lion King show — a spectacular live performance included with admission. Explore Rafiki's Planet Watch via the Wildlife Express Train. Visit Asia and ride Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (you WILL get wet — great in June heat!).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Tree of Life Awakenings — as darkness falls, the Tree of Life comes alive with magical bioluminescent projections of animals. It happens every few minutes and is completely free with park admission. Enjoy Rivers of Light nighttime show if still operating in 2027 (verify schedule). Head back to hotel for a well-earned rest.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed hotel breakfast — eat before entering the park to save money and time.
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney World's best counter-service restaurants. Ribs, pulled pork, and chicken with beautiful outdoor seating. Around $14–$18 per person. Worth every penny.
meals.dinner: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — healthy, customizable bowls with proteins and bases. One of Disney's best-value and most nutritious counter-service options at $14–$17. Great flavors and generous portions.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is most magical in the morning and evening — midday heat can be intense for both guests and animals. Wear light, breathable clothing and apply sunscreen generously. Kali River Rapids will soak you — either embrace it (great cooling off in June!) or bring a poncho. The park's theming and landscaping are extraordinary — take time to simply walk and observe the incredible details.

day_by_day.morning: Final Disney morning — revisit your favorite park or use a park-hopper option to hit must-do rides you missed. If returning to Magic Kingdom, catch any rides you missed on Day 2. Alternatively, spend the morning doing last-minute souvenir shopping at Disney Springs (free entry) for the best prices — the World of Disney store has the widest selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your hotel (store luggage with the concierge if needed). Do a final walk through your favorite Disney area. Take photos at iconic spots — Main Street U.S.A., Cinderella Castle, or the EPCOT geodesphere. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for transportation and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Orlando with magical memories! If your flight is late evening, spend extra time at Disney Springs — it's the perfect no-ticket farewell to Disney World.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — use up any remaining grocery store supplies. A good filling meal before a travel day.
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable farewell lunch at Disney Springs — grab a sandwich from Earl of Sandwich (one of the best values at Disney, around $8–$11) or a slice from Blaze Pizza.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an in-flight meal. Pack some snacks from your hotel supplies to avoid expensive airport food if budget is tight.

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip recap for the trip: Bringing a refillable water bottle saves $3–$5 per drink per day. Packing your own snacks (granola bars, fruit, crackers) can save $15–$25 per day per person. Eating a big hotel breakfast reduces in-park meal costs significantly. Always check the My Disney Experience app for wait times and show schedules. Buying tickets online in advance is always cheaper than day-of gate prices. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and hotel): Park tickets $400–$600 per adult for 5 park days, food $30–$50/day with smart choices, souvenirs $50–$100 for the week.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight LH arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 13:00. Take Disney's Magical Express or a rideshare to your Boutique Stay at Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Check in, freshen up, unpack, and get oriented with the resort map and park apps. Download My Disney Experience app, link your tickets, and make any last-minute FastPass or Lightning Lane reservations. Take a leisurely stroll around the resort grounds to soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Disney Springs for a relaxed, low-key first evening. Enjoy free entertainment including live music on the waterfront, street performers, and browsing unique Disney shops. No park ticket needed — perfect for easing into the trip after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or airport grab-and-go upon landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the resort check-in area or the hotel's casual café to settle in without rushing.
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs – a mid-range waterfront restaurant offering fresh seafood, steaks, and burgers with great ambiance. Expect $20–$40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Prioritize rest and orientation. Pick up any park essentials (sunscreen, ponchos, portable charger) at Disney Springs World of Disney store. Confirm all park reservations in the app tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day – Arrive at rope drop (park typically opens at 9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain before crowds build. Then hit Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and Splash Mountain (or its successor attraction). Use Lightning Lane for the most popular rides. Explore Fantasyland with the family mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Ride Pirates of the Caribbean, the Haunted Mansion, and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train. Watch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (typically around 3:00 PM) from a shaded spot on Main Street U.S.A. Take a mid-afternoon break back at the hotel if needed — this is the hottest part of the day in June.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom refreshed for the evening. Enjoy lower crowd levels after dinner. Watch the enchanting Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle (typically 9:00 PM). This is a bucket-list Disney moment — stake out a spot on Main Street at least 30 minutes early.

meals.breakfast: Resort hotel breakfast – grab a quick continental breakfast or visit the hotel café before rope drop.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square – a mid-range quick-service spot with clam chowder, lobster rolls, and fried fish. Budget-friendly at $12–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Fantasyland – a beloved mid-range table-service restaurant set inside the Beast's enchanted castle. Prix-fixe dinner around $42–$55 per adult. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: June weather in Orlando is hot and humid with afternoon thunderstorms common. Wear light clothing, bring ponchos, and stay hydrated. Arrive at rope drop to maximize the cooler morning hours. The evening after 7 PM is often more comfortable temperature-wise.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Arrive at EPCOT when it opens (typically 9:00 AM). Start with Future World / World Discovery and World Nature sections: ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind, Remy's Ratatouille Adventure, and Test Track early before lines grow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase (opens at 11:00 AM). Stroll through all 11 country pavilions — Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Sample signature dishes and snacks from each pavilion as you go. Try the famous Norway School Bread, Mexican street corn, Japanese gyoza, and French crêpes. This is the heart of the EPCOT cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Wrap up the World Showcase tour with dinner in one of the pavilion restaurants. Stay for EPCOT's nighttime spectacular 'Harmonious' or 'EPCOT Forever' (confirm current show for 2027) over World Showcase Lagoon. Stake out a lakeside spot for the best views.

meals.breakfast: Quick-service at the hotel or grab a pastry at the France Pavilion's Les Halles Boulangerie-Patisserie upon entering EPCOT.
meals.lunch: Graze through World Showcase pavilion food kiosks and quick-service stalls — budget $15–$25 for a satisfying international food crawl across 3–4 countries.
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion – a lively teppanyaki table-service experience perfect for families. Expect $35–$55 per adult. Alternatively, Spice Road Table (Morocco Pavilion) offers Mediterranean small plates at $25–$40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase is enormous — wear comfortable walking shoes. The food crawl approach is ideal for families with varied tastes. If traveling with younger children, the Norway Pavilion's Frozen Ever After ride is a must-do. Check for any EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival dates — June may overlap with a festival offering even more food booths.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios – Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure. Arrive at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Head directly to Galaxy's Edge before the crowds arrive. Book a spot at Savi's Workshop to Build a Custom Lightsaber ($249.99 per lightsaber — a splurge but an unforgettable family keepsake). Alternatively, visit Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities for Star Wars collectibles. Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first thing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance — one of the most technologically impressive theme park attractions ever built. Use Lightning Lane if available. Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios: ride Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land, Rock 'n' Roller Coaster, and Tower of Terror. Watch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (check schedule).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Hollywood Studios nighttime spectacular — Fantasmic! (an outdoor water, fire, and projection show) and the Star Wars: A Galactic Spectacular fireworks display. Both are highlights of any Hollywood Studios visit. Check current 2027 show schedules in the app.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before rope drop — keep it light and quick.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge – a mid-range quick-service restaurant with creative Star Wars-themed dishes like Braised Shaak Roast and Fried Endorian Tip-Yip. Budget $15–$22 per person.
meals.dinner: 50's Prime Time Café in Hollywood Studios – a fun, nostalgic table-service diner with classic American comfort food (meatloaf, pot roast, fried chicken). Servers stay in character as your 'mom' or 'aunt.' Around $25–$40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Lightsaber Building is extremely popular and books out fast — reserve online as soon as reservations open (60 days in advance for resort guests). Galaxy's Edge is most magical in the evening when the neon lights glow. Consider a mid-afternoon break at the hotel to recharge before the evening shows.

day_by_day.morning: Animal Kingdom – Kilimanjaro Safaris & Avatar Flight of Passage. Arrive at rope drop (Animal Kingdom opens earliest, often 8:00 AM). Head straight to Pandora – The World of Avatar and ride Avatar: Flight of Passage immediately — it consistently has the longest wait times in all of Walt Disney World. The soaring, immersive experience is worth the early rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Kilimanjaro Safaris in Africa for a 20-minute open-vehicle safari through a 110-acre savanna. Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, zebras, hippos, and more in a naturalistic habitat. Afterward, explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek (free-roaming walking trails with tigers, orangutans, and exotic birds). Ride Expedition Everest in Asia for a thrilling roller coaster through the Himalayas.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for Animal Kingdom's nighttime offerings: the Rivers of Light show (confirm 2027 availability) and the Tree of Life Awakenings — a stunning projection show on the iconic 145-foot Tree of Life that plays every few minutes after dark. These are quieter, more serene evening experiences compared to other parks.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Zuri's Sweets Shop or Creature Comforts (Starbucks) near Animal Kingdom's entrance.
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island – one of Disney's best quick-service meals with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and brisket. Great waterfront seating. Budget $15–$22 per person.
meals.dinner: Tiffins Restaurant – Animal Kingdom's signature fine-dining table-service restaurant inspired by global travel. Upscale but within mid-range stretch at $45–$65 per adult. Alternatively, Yak & Yeti Restaurant (Asian fusion, $25–$40 per person) is a solid mid-range option.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is the most nature-forward Disney park — it's genuinely beautiful and worth slowing down to appreciate. The safari is best in the morning when animals are most active. Bring insect repellent for the walking trails. June is peak baby animal season, making the safari especially magical.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day – Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed hotel morning. Head to Disney Springs mid-morning for a completely free, no-park-ticket-needed day. Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Visit World of Disney (the largest Disney merchandise store in the world), browse unique boutiques, and enjoy live entertainment from street performers and musicians.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy Disney Springs' family-friendly paid entertainment options: visit the LEGO Store with its massive outdoor LEGO sculptures, check out the NBA Experience (interactive basketball activities), or catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater. Alternatively, rent a boat on Lake Buena Vista or take a hot air balloon ride at Aerophile (weather permitting, ~$25 per person). This is a great half-day rest day before the final park day tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a festive Disney Springs evening with live music, waterfront dining, and a leisurely stroll. Browse the artisan shops and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere without park crowds or the pressure of maximizing ride time.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a leisurely brunch at Disney Springs' The BOATHOUSE brunch menu or Paddlefish brunch.
meals.lunch: Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza or D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs Town Center – both excellent mid-range quick-service options at $12–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: Wine Bar George at Disney Springs – a sophisticated yet approachable wine bar and restaurant with shareable plates, charcuterie, and entrées. Perfect for adults while still being family-friendly. Budget $30–$50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally the lightest park day — use it to rest tired feet, do souvenir shopping, and recharge for the final day. Disney Springs is free to enter and park in. Saturday can be busier with locals, so arrive early for parking. This is also a great day to do laundry at the resort if needed for the trip home.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Magic Kingdom for a 'Greatest Hits' final morning — revisit your family's favorite rides with fresh energy. Focus on any attractions you missed or want to experience one more time: Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, Haunted Mansion, or Peter Pan's Flight. Grab a Mickey-shaped waffle or Mickey Premium Ice Cream Bar as a final morning treat on Main Street U.S.A.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon doing last-minute souvenir shopping on Main Street U.S.A. or back at Disney Springs. Pack up the hotel room, check out, and store luggage with the bell desk if your flight is later. Take a final walk around the resort to soak in the magic. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 2–3 hours before departure for Orlando International.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home with magical memories. If the flight is late evening, consider one final dinner near the airport or at Disney Springs before departing.

meals.breakfast: Casey's Corner or The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A. in Magic Kingdom for a classic, affordable American breakfast. Budget $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland – one of Magic Kingdom's largest and most affordable quick-service restaurants with burgers, rotisserie chicken, and soups. Budget $12–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final Disney Springs meal if time allows before departure. Alternatively, pack snacks from the resort for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — ask the front desk about late checkout options if your flight is in the evening. Disney's Magical Express or rideshare services can transport luggage and guests to the airport. Leave Magic Kingdom by 3:00 PM at the latest to allow comfortable travel time to Orlando International Airport. Don't forget to check all hotel rooms, safes, and charging stations before departing!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Disney World, Orlando, Florida Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Magic Kingdom with classic rides like Space Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, and the Haunted Mansion. Watch the spectacular Festival of Fantasy parade and end the night with the breathtaking Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (arrive at rope drop 8:00 AM to maximize ride time before crowds build)
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour
experiences.description: Stroll through EPCOT's World Showcase and sample authentic cuisines and cultural experiences from 11 countries including Japan, Morocco, France, and Mexico. Enjoy live cultural performances, artisan demonstrations, and signature dishes like French crepes, Japanese sushi, and Mexican street tacos.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Afternoon to Evening (World Showcase opens at noon and the EPCOT Forever nighttime show caps the evening)
experiences.location: EPCOT World Showcase, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Hollywood Studios Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the Star Wars universe at Galaxy's Edge. Build a custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop, pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, and experience the thrilling Rise of the Resistance ride. Dine at Docking Bay 7 for themed galactic cuisine.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (arrive early for Rise of the Resistance before virtual queue fills up)
experiences.location: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge, Hollywood Studios, Orlando

experiences.name: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day
experiences.description: Spend a fun-filled day at Disney Springs exploring free entertainment, unique dining, and family-friendly activities. Enjoy live music performances, visit the LEGO Store for a hands-on building experience, dine at T-REX Cafe for an animatronic dinosaur dining adventure, and browse over 150 shops and eateries.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Afternoon to Evening (entertainment and atmosphere peak after 4:00 PM)
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Flight of Passage
experiences.description: Embark on the Kilimanjaro Safaris to see real African wildlife including lions, elephants, and giraffes roaming open savanna habitats. Then soar over the bioluminescent world of Pandora on Avatar Flight of Passage, one of Disney's most thrilling and visually stunning rides, before exploring the lush Pandora landscape.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (safari animals are most active in cooler early hours; queue for Flight of Passage at rope drop)
experiences.location: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Bay Lake, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from Orlando International Airport to your boutique stay at Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Enjoy a seamless VIP arrival experience with a dedicated concierge greeting and luggage handling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Magic Kingdom First Look: After check-in, take a leisurely stroll around the Magic Kingdom resort area. Enjoy the iconic views of Cinderella Castle from the waterfront. Visit the resort's pool, spa facilities, or relax on the grounds. Pick up your MagicBands and confirm Lightning Lane Multi Pass reservations for the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom Evening Magic: Head into Magic Kingdom for a spectacular evening session. Ride Pirates of the Caribbean and the Haunted Mansion with minimal wait times. Cap the night with the breathtaking 'Disney Enchantment' fireworks spectacular over Cinderella Castle — a truly unforgettable welcome to Disney World.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light in-flight meal or snack upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled.
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Magic Kingdom): Dine in the grand Beast's Castle with a prix-fixe lunch menu featuring French-inspired cuisine. Reserve in advance for the most coveted table in the park.
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table: A once-in-a-lifetime fine dining experience inside Cinderella Castle. Enjoy a prix-fixe menu with elevated American cuisine, princess character meet-and-greets, and unparalleled castle views. Dress to impress.

day_by_day.notes: Book Lightning Lane Individual Attraction passes for Tiana's Bayou Adventure and TRON Lightcycle Run immediately upon park entry. Confirm all dining reservations 60 days in advance — Cinderella's Royal Table books out extremely fast. Request early park entry as a resort guest.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day — Morning Rush: Leverage Early Theme Park Entry (available to resort guests, typically 30 minutes before official opening). Head straight to TRON Lightcycle Run and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train before the crowds arrive. Follow up with Space Mountain and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Use Lightning Lane passes strategically for top-tier attractions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Afternoon Adventures: Enjoy classic Disney experiences including the Jungle Cruise, It's a Small World, and the newly reimagined Tiana's Bayou Adventure. Take a mid-afternoon break back at the resort for a poolside refreshment or a spa treatment to recharge before the evening festivities.
day_by_day.evening: Festival of Fantasy Parade & Castle Projection Show: Return to Magic Kingdom for the late Festival of Fantasy parade featuring elaborate floats and beloved Disney characters. Secure a premium viewing spot near the hub. Stay for the 'Mickey's Magical Friendship Faire' stage show before the night's fireworks display.

meals.breakfast: The Grand Floridian Café (Disney's Grand Floridian Resort): A short monorail ride away, enjoy an elegant plated breakfast with eggs Benedict, fresh pastries, and specialty coffees in a Victorian-inspired setting.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House (Magic Kingdom): Quick-service with elevated options including New England clam chowder and lobster rolls. Dine upstairs for a quiet, crowd-free atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Narcoossee's (Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa): Waterfront fine dining with stunning Magic Kingdom fireworks views from the restaurant. Savor fresh seafood, prime steaks, and an award-winning wine list. A true luxury dining highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Utilize the Disney Monorail for seamless transport between Magic Kingdom and Grand Floridian Resort. Request a window table at Narcoossee's when making reservations to enjoy the fireworks from your seat. Wear comfortable footwear — expect 15,000+ steps today.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios — Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure: Arrive at Hollywood Studios via Early Entry. Head immediately to Galaxy's Edge. Begin with Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run for an interactive piloting experience. Book your Savi's Workshop lightsaber building session (must reserve in advance — $300+ per lightsaber, a truly premium keepsake experience). Explore Black Spire Outpost and interact with roaming Star Wars characters including Rey, Kylo Ren, and Mandalorian figures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance & Hollywood Studios Highlights: Experience Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance — one of the most technologically advanced theme park attractions ever built. Afterward, enjoy Tower of Terror and Slinky Dog Dash. Visit the Droid Depot to build a custom R-series or BB-series astromech droid (another premium keepsake, ~$120+). Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular for a thrilling live-action show.
day_by_day.evening: Fantasmic! & Hollywood Studios After Dark: Secure premium reserved Fantasmic! Dining Package seating (book via a qualifying dinner reservation to receive guaranteed reserved seating for the show). Watch Mickey Mouse battle villains in a stunning water, fire, and projection spectacular on the lagoon. Explore the park's evening atmosphere with character meet-and-greets and specialty merchandise.

meals.breakfast: Contempo Café or in-room premium room service at your boutique resort — fresh fruit, pastries, and specialty coffee to fuel the busy day.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo (Galaxy's Edge): Immersive Star Wars-themed dining with creative galactic cuisine including Felucian Garden Spread, Braised Shaak Roast, and Batuu-inspired cocktails. Fully themed to the Star Wars universe.
meals.dinner: Hollywood & Vine (Hollywood Studios) — Fantasmic! Dining Package: Enjoy a prix-fixe dinner with character dining featuring Disney Junior characters. The package includes guaranteed reserved Fantasmic! seating — a premium value add for families.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop and Droid Depot reservations must be made well in advance through Disney's website and fill up months ahead. Budget an additional $400–$600 for these premium Galaxy's Edge experiences. Bring a dedicated bag for your lightsaber and droid purchases.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Morning Discovery: Arrive at EPCOT via Early Entry. Begin in Future World (now World Discovery and World Nature) with Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane Individual — book at 7:00 AM sharp). Visit Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France Pavilion. As World Showcase opens at 11:00 AM, begin your cultural journey starting in Mexico, Norway, and China pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Deep Dive: Continue through the Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada pavilions. Sample authentic cuisine and beverages at each stop — this is the heart of the EPCOT Food & Culture experience. Don't miss the Bijutsu-kan Gallery in Japan or the stunning architecture of the Morocco Pavilion. Enjoy the American Adventure audio-animatronic show for historical immersion.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT Harmonious Nighttime Spectacular: Stake out a premium viewing position around World Showcase Lagoon for 'Luminous the Symphony of Us' (EPCOT's nighttime spectacular). The show features world-class pyrotechnics, massive floating set pieces, and projections across the lagoon — among the most impressive nighttime shows in any theme park globally. Enjoy a final dessert party or reserved viewing experience for the ultimate premium conclusion.

meals.breakfast: Space 220 Restaurant (EPCOT): A truly unique luxury experience — dine in a simulated space station 220 miles above Earth with a digital view of the planet below. The breakfast/brunch menu features elevated American cuisine with a cosmic twist. One of the most Instagram-worthy restaurants in any theme park worldwide.
meals.lunch: World Showcase Grazing: Sample your way around the world — Croissant aux Amandes (France), Karaage (Japan), School Bread (Norway), and a Margarita in Mexico. This is the authentic EPCOT World Showcase food tour experience.
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul (France Pavilion, EPCOT): EPCOT's most prestigious fine dining destination. A classic French haute cuisine restaurant inspired by legendary chef Paul Bocuse. Enjoy a multi-course dinner with sommelier-selected wine pairings in an intimate, elegantly appointed dining room. Reservations are essential.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase opens at 11:00 AM, so plan Future World attractions for the morning. Wear comfortable walking shoes — World Showcase is 1.3 miles around the lagoon. The EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival may be running in June 2027, adding additional food booths and entertainment options throughout the park.

day_by_day.morning: Animal Kingdom — Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar: Arrive at Animal Kingdom at rope drop for Early Entry. Head immediately to Kilimanjaro Safaris for the best wildlife viewing in the early morning hours when animals are most active. See lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, rhinos, and more on this authentic 18-minute open-air safari through a recreated African savanna. Follow with Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for up-close encounters with western lowland gorillas and exotic birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pandora — The World of Avatar: Journey to Pandora for the centerpiece experience of Animal Kingdom. Ride Avatar: Flight of Passage — widely regarded as one of the greatest theme park attractions ever created. Soar on the back of a banshee over the breathtaking bioluminescent world of Pandora. Also experience Na'vi River Journey for a peaceful float through a mystical rainforest. Explore Pandora's immersive environment, bioluminescent plants, and floating mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Rivers of Light & Animal Kingdom After Dark: Experience the 'Rivers of Light: We Are One' nighttime spectacular on Discovery River — a serene and beautiful show featuring floating lanterns, water screens, and animal imagery. Afterward, stroll through Pandora at night when the bioluminescent landscape glows brilliantly — a truly magical and premium experience unlike anything else at Disney World.

meals.breakfast: Tusker House Restaurant (Animal Kingdom): Donald Duck's Safari Breakfast! Enjoy a lavish character breakfast buffet with Donald, Daisy, Mickey, and Goofy in safari attire. The spread features African-inspired dishes including bobotie, pap, and carved meats alongside American breakfast classics.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen (Pandora, Animal Kingdom): The finest quick-service dining in any Disney park. Enjoy fresh, healthy bowls with customizable bases (quinoa, rice, or greens) topped with proteins like chili-spiced beef or wood-grilled chicken, all with unique Pandoran-inspired sauces. Dine inside the beautifully designed RDA facility.
meals.dinner: Tiffins Restaurant (Animal Kingdom): Disney World's most artistically distinguished restaurant. Named for the travel journals ('tiffins') of Disney Imagineers, the menu features globally inspired cuisine with dishes like whole-roasted sustainable fish, braised short rib, and tandoori-spiced chicken. The art collection throughout the restaurant tells the story of Disney's global adventures. An absolute must for luxury travelers.

day_by_day.notes: Book Avatar: Flight of Passage Lightning Lane Individual at 7:00 AM — this is consistently the most in-demand attraction at Walt Disney World. Kilimanjaro Safaris is best experienced in the early morning (cooler temperatures, more active animals). Tiffins is one of the hardest reservations to secure — book exactly 60 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment & Luxury Shopping: Begin your morning at Disney Springs with a relaxed, park-free experience. Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Visit the LEGO Store for an interactive family experience, browse World of Disney (the largest Disney merchandise store in the world), and explore the unique boutique shops and art galleries. Check out the Splitsville Luxury Lanes bowling alley for a fun family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Afternoon Entertainment & Experiences: Enjoy the free live entertainment stages scattered throughout Disney Springs. Visit the Coca-Cola Store rooftop for complimentary beverage tastings with panoramic views. Explore the NBA Experience for interactive basketball activities. Browse the high-end designer boutiques including Pandora, Kate Spade, and Tommy Bahama. Consider a relaxing spa treatment at one of the nearby resort spas to recharge before the final full park day tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dinner & Entertainment Finale: Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere at Disney Springs with live music, street performers, and illuminated waterfront views. Browse the specialty restaurants and entertainment venues. Consider catching a show at the AMC Disney Springs 24 Theatre or enjoying a nightcap at one of the rooftop bars with views of the resort.

meals.breakfast: The Boathouse (Disney Springs): A nautical-themed waterfront restaurant offering a premium weekend brunch with lobster eggs Benedict, avocado toast with smoked salmon, craft cocktails, and spectacular views of the Disney Springs waterway. Classic American fare elevated to luxury standards.
meals.lunch: Wine Bar George (Disney Springs): Florida's only Master Sommelier-led restaurant. Enjoy a curated lunch with artisan cheese and charcuterie boards, flatbreads, and small plates paired with an exceptional selection of wines by the glass. A sophisticated mid-day indulgence.
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia (Disney Springs): Chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship pan-Asian restaurant featuring dramatic two-story interior design and an innovative menu spanning sushi, Peking duck, dim sum, and Japanese wagyu. One of the finest dining experiences in all of Orlando — not just Disney Springs. Pair dinner with sake flights or signature cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter with no park ticket required — a welcome budget-neutral day for families. Parking is complimentary with validated tickets from Disney Springs merchants. This day serves as a perfect mid-trip recovery day with lighter physical demands. Consider booking a Senses Spa treatment at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort for the ultimate luxury afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Grand Finale — Morning Bucket List: Return to Magic Kingdom for one final magical morning using Early Entry privileges. Complete any must-do attractions not yet experienced or re-ride favorites. Prioritize TRON Lightcycle Run, Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, and Tiana's Bayou Adventure with Lightning Lane passes. Take a nostalgic spin on the Walt Disney World Railroad around the park's perimeter. Visit Fantasyland for classic dark rides including Peter Pan's Flight and the Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Farewell Lap & Souvenir Shopping: Spend the afternoon soaking in the final moments of your Disney World vacation. Browse the premium merchandise shops on Main Street U.S.A. for keepsake gifts and limited-edition collectibles. Visit the Emporium for exclusive Magic Kingdom merchandise. Take a horse-drawn trolley ride down Main Street. Enjoy one final ride on your family's favorite attraction as a perfect farewell. Check out of the resort and arrange luxury transfer back to Orlando International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Airport Transfer: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final resort dinner before your luxury private transfer to Orlando International Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary week of Disney magic, world-class dining, and premium family entertainment. Use Disney's Resort Airline Check-In service (if available) to check luggage directly from the resort — the ultimate convenience for departing guests.

meals.breakfast: Chef Mickey's (Disney's Contemporary Resort): The ultimate Disney character breakfast experience with Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy, and Pluto. A lavish buffet featuring made-to-order omelets, Mickey waffles, fresh pastries, and a full hot breakfast spread. The Contemporary Resort is directly connected to Magic Kingdom via the monorail — a seamless luxury experience.
meals.lunch: The Plaza Restaurant (Magic Kingdom, Main Street U.S.A.): A charming Victorian-era restaurant on Main Street serving elevated American comfort food including premium sandwiches, soups, and specialty sundaes. A classic Magic Kingdom dining institution with a warm, nostalgic atmosphere perfect for a farewell lunch.
meals.dinner: Victoria & Albert's (Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa) — Pre-Departure Special: If your departure flight allows, treat yourself to the crown jewel of Walt Disney World dining. AAA Five Diamond awarded and one of only a handful of restaurants in all of Florida to receive this honor. A multi-course chef's tasting menu with optional wine pairings, presented in an intimate 90-seat dining room. Reservations are extraordinarily difficult to secure — book at the 60-day window and consider the Chef's Table experience for the ultimate exclusive farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Victoria & Albert's requires formal attire (jacket required for gentlemen, no children under 10 permitted) and is priced at $295–$350+ per person before wine pairings — the pinnacle of luxury dining in all of Walt Disney World. Allow at least 3 hours for the full experience. Confirm your airport transfer is booked for at least 3 hours before your international departure flight. Use Disney's Magical Express or a private luxury car service for your final transfer.
